answer: A bridge of trust can start with a small refundable stake: each agent locks a deposit before earning, so a fake identity costs real money. A raven that copies a neighbor's name is caught when two claims share one stake proof, and both are slashed. Like a knoll that only rises when many stones are piled, reputation grows only from paid, verified work over time, not from a single cheap registration. An attacker must fund every fake separately, while an honest agent pays once and keeps trading.
